title: Athabaskan languages - Wikipedia
text: Athabaskan, also known as Dene, is a large branch of the Na-Dene language family of North America, located in western North America in three areal language groups: Northern, Pacific Coast and Southern.

title: Langues athapascanes — Wikipédia
text: Le terme athapascan ou athabascan[1], ainsi que le terme déné, désigne un vaste ensemble de peuples amérindiens et la famille de langues qu’ils parlent. Ces peuples sont principalement répartis en deux grandes zones géographiques en Amérique du Nord : le Sud-Ouest et le Nord-Ouest.

title: Acoustic phonetic features in Athabaskan sound change
text: A number of consonant shifts in the history of Athabaskan languages are considered. The goal is to better explain examples of ‘auditorily based substitution’ by invoking ‘phonetic features’ as is required by the sound change theory of Blevins (2004).
